name: Amir Jain
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember learning to cook an old neighbor's strange idea of breakfast.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Amir by a small Friday habit. Amir pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I learned the meal routine because I wanted to flirt with the neighbor and ended up loving Wednesdays.
appearance: Amir has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Amir folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Amir has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To keep the Wednesday meal shared.
family: Amanda Wong is Amir’s half-sibling. Amir chooses whether to use it. Amanda saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Nine unpaid hours*, Amanda says, “I counted overtime for everyone except myself.”
connections: Benedict Holt. The neighbor who enjoys Wednesdays helps the family let the carer come home without a report.

reactions.situation: The carer's Wednesday relief calls in sick
reactions.response: Amir tells the carer plainly how much of Wednesday can still be covered.

reactions.situation: A street musician can't finish a familiar song
reactions.response: Amir starts a quiet conversation with the most impatient onlookers so the musician can recover their own time.

reactions.response: Amir explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
reactions.asWritten: If accused of favoritism, Amir explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
